subject: Continuity validation: multi-site RTO/RPO acceptance & demo scheduling
messages:
From: Daniel Reyes <daniel.reyes@pioneerhealth.org>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@pioneerhealth.org>
Date: Thu, 12 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pioneer Health - clarifications on RTO/RPO obligations and acceptance testing

Hi Vivek / Ben,

Thanks for the RFP response — we reviewed the continuity section and had a couple of clarifying asks before we move to the contract stage. Specifically:

1) You list supported RTOs of 60s for read-heavy inference and 5 minutes for full routing to a secondary region. Can you confirm whether the 60s is a per-request tail-latency SLA during a node-level failure, or an application-level availability target?

2) For RPO you mention eventual consistency with prefix/KV cache warmup. What is the expected data exposure window for customer-provided KV caches during a regional switchover? We need a number we can present to compliance (seconds/minutes).

3) We also want to run an on-site (remote) continuity validation window with Redwood engineers: a failover demo + controlled service failover to our secondary region. Please propose a test plan and two candidate dates.

Attached: Pioneer_H_SOW_review_annotated.pdf (high level comments).

Best,
Daniel
Director, Infrastructure Operations
Pioneer Health

---
Attachment: Pioneer_H_SOW_review_annotated.pdf (application/pdf stub)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Reyes <daniel.reyes@pioneerhealth.org>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jul 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pioneer Health - clarifications on RTO/RPO obligations and acceptance testing

Hi Daniel — thanks for the clear asks. Short answers up-front, full plan below and a proposed test window.

1) The 60s callout is a per-request recovery target for a degraded-serving scenario (single-node GPU failure) where traffic is drained and remapped to remaining capacity; it is not the contract-wide uptime SLA. The contractual availability SLA is specified separately in Section 5.2 of the SOW (99.9% monthly).

2) Expected RPO for customer KV material (prefix cache) during a region switchover is: typical warmup exposure of 2–5 minutes for active traffic patterns; worst-case (cold caches) up to 15 minutes while prefix traffic rehydrates. We will add explicit language in the SOW appendix.

3) Proposed continuity validation: 90-minute remote session — 30m review, 30m simulated partial failure + KV-warmup observation, 30m full regional failover to our secondary region with traffic verification. Candidate dates: Mon Jul 23 or Thu Jul 26 (US business hours).

I attached the Redwood RTO/RPO profile and a short demo runbook; Ben will follow up on logistics and instrumentation we will expose during the test (metrics and trace links).

Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Reliability, Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com

---
Attachments: redwood_rto_rpo_profile_v1.pdf (application/pdf stub); failover-demo-runbook.md (text/markdown stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Reyes <daniel.reyes@pioneerhealth.org>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jul 2028 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pioneer Health - clarifications on RTO/RPO obligations and acceptance testing

Daniel — looping in a concise checklist we'll use during the session and what you'll see in the telemetry:

- Pre-test: baseline token/sec and tail latency capture (5m window).
- Step 1 (node degradation): artificially terminate one serving shard; observe request routing and per-token latency; expected median latency bump < 20% and tail percentiles recover in < 60s.
- Step 2 (prefix cache eviction): clear prefix cache on a canary namespace and replay representative traffic for 10m; expect cache rehydration profile: 80% within 2–5m.
- Step 3 (regional failover): simulate region outage and switch routing policy to secondary (automated routing + model variant fallback); verify end-to-end success rate and data sync status. Expected RPO window: up to 15 minutes worst-case; typical 2–5 minutes.

Instrumentation exposed during test: per-request traces, per-model KV cache hit/miss rates, per-region request counters, and an ephemeral Prometheus scrape target we'll stand up for the test.

Please confirm which of the two dates works and whether you need a day-break or weekend slot (we can provide engineers off-hours under an escalation arrangement).

—Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@pioneerhealth.org>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Reyes <daniel.reyes@pioneerhealth.org>, Procurement Team <procurement@pioneerhealth.org>
Date: Fri, 13 Jul 2028 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pioneer Health - clarifications on RTO/RPO obligations and acceptance testing

Thanks Ben — the checklist looks good. Two quick follow-ups:

- For the regional failover do you require a network cutover on our side (BGP) or can this be a purely application-level reroute? We prefer minimal network changes during a demo.
- Procurement requests a short acceptance criteria paragraph we can attach to the PO: we need one-sentence statements for RTO (regional failover) and RPO for inclusion in the contract appendix.

We prefer Jul 26 afternoon (US ET) for the session. Also — can you provide the anticipated changes to session metrics we should expect so our monitoring can be aligned?

Best,
Alicia Gomez
Sourcing Manager, Pioneer Health

Date: Fri, 13 Jul 2028 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pioneer Health - clarifications on RTO/RPO obligations and acceptance testing

Alicia — short answers to help Procurement:

• Network cutover: demonstration will use application-level routing (no BGP changes required). We'll use our control plane to shift traffic and show the routing policy change; we can coordinate IP-level options if you want a deeper exercise, but it's not required for acceptance.

• Acceptance-criteria blurbs you can add to the PO:
  - RTO (regional failover): "Redwood will execute region failover with application routing to secondary region; customer-observed service availability will be restored within 5 minutes under standard traffic patterns."
  - RPO (customer KV/cache): "Typical prefix cache rehydration observed within 2–5 minutes; worst-case exposure up to 15 minutes while caches rehydrate. Persistent customer data (cloud storage) is not impacted by cache rehydration timelines."

Ben — we'll also include a short expected-metrics list: overall success rate > 99.5% during the failover, error-rate spike limited to < 1.5% transient, and a tail-latency recovery to baseline within 5 minutes post-switch.

I've added a calendar invite for Jul 26 14:00 ET (attached). Monica will coordinate access to the ephemeral metrics endpoint.

Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
